ActiveSite.description:
A site or site ensemble held responsible for catalysis (metal step, oxide vacancy, metal-oxide
interface, acid site, single atom). Its identity is usually an interpretation: HAS_SITE carries
the epistemic status.

Analysis.description:
A calculation or fit reported by a source or made on reported data: an equilibrium constant, a
kinetic fit (apparent activation energy, reaction orders), a transport-limitation check
(Weisz-Prater, Mears), with the conditions it applies to and its results.

Catalyst.description: A catalyst formulation as its source names it ("Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 44:36:20 wt", "zinc chromite"). Its make-up is HAS_COMPONENT edges to species and materials, each with its role (active phase, support, promoter, binder, dopant) and fraction; its phases are HAS_PHASE; physical specimens are CatalystSamples (HAS_FORMULATION). There are no role labels: a support is a Material, a promoter a ChemicalSpecies, and the role is on the edge.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

properties.description: Stated properties other than composition (component ratios, masses, loadings).

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

CatalystSample.description:
A physical specimen of a catalyst: the batch, or part of a batch, that was prepared, treated,
tested and characterized. It carries the preparation and treatment history; its state at a
given time is on the edge that uses it. Batch identity is asserted only when the source states it.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

CatalystState.description:
The structure and composition a catalyst sample (or a model of it) is in at a stated point of
an action sequence: after a pretreatment, during a reaction at a stated pressure or potential,
after a gas switch. It is the answer to "which phase is in effect": its phases are HAS_PHASE
edges to Materials (with location and dominance), what it is a state of is STATE_OF, the action
it is reached by is REACHED_BY (with the timing), and the characterizations or computations that
establish it are DETERMINED_BY. A test measured in the state is IN_STATE. A state predicted by a
simulation has origin computed. The state is a record of what the source reports, not an
equilibrium assignment.

conditions.description: The environment the state is observed in (temperature, total or partial pressures, potential).

dynamics.description: What the catalyst is observed doing in this state.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

morphology.description: The structure in words, as the source gives it ("MoCx overlayers on β-Mo2N").

persistence.description: kinetically_trapped = persists although another state is expected to be stable (e.g. an oxide kept alongside metal for hours).

properties.description: Stated values of the state (phase fractions, surface atomic ratios, onset temperatures).

regime.description: drifting = still changing when observed (e.g. an oxide dissolving over hours); oscillatory = repeatedly switching or fluctuating.

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

state_kind.description: working = under reaction conditions; post_reaction = after the action, outside it (e.g. cooled, transferred).

CatalyticTest.description: One reported catalytic test: a catalyst sample (USES_CATALYST), a feed (FED_WITH), a reactor (IN_REACTOR) and a reaction (OF_REACTION), driven by one or more driving forces, with the conditions and results the source gives. Declared conditions and results are properties; others go in the inherited conditions and results maps. Driving-force properties (potential, irradiance, discharge power) come from the vocabulary of their driving force. A reported equilibrium estimate is a CatalyticTest with test_kind equilibrium_estimate and experiment_kind computational.

Hypothesis.description:
A conjectured, testable statement about how or why the studied system behaves. It is not a
finding: experiments TEST it, and its standing follows from the outcomes. Conclusions about it
are Claims ABOUT it; accumulating support does not turn it into a Claim.

hypothesis_kind.description: auxiliary = an assumption needed to derive predictions; competing = an alternative explanation (a confounder, a bias, a design effect).

proposed_at.description: When the hypothesis was first proposed (from the source), not when it was recorded.

refuted_if.description: What observation would refute it, when stated.

statistical_role.description: EXPO NullHypothesis H0 / alternative H1, when the hypothesis is tested statistically.

IlluminatedCell.description: An electrochemical cell built to be illuminated: the light reaches the electrogenerated species in solution; whether the electrode itself is shielded from the light decides whether photoelectrochemistry at the electrode can be ruled out.

LightSource.description: What illuminates a photo-driven experiment: the lamp, LED, laser or sun, its spectrum, filters and nominal power. The irradiance at the sample is a property of the experiment.

spectrum.description: The emission spectrum or standard (e.g. AM1.5G) as stated.

Material.description:
A material identity: a solid's composition with its crystal structure or stated non-crystalline
form (wurtzite ZnO, gamma-Al2O3, ZnCr2O4 spinel, fcc Cu, amorphous silica, MFI zeolite). The
counterpart of ChemicalSpecies for solids: Al2O3 is one ChemicalSpecies but several Materials.
Domains declare the roles a material plays (in catalysis, a catalyst or a support);
the Material is what such a role node is made of. A support, binder or other solid a catalyst is made with is a Material; its role in the catalyst is on HAS_COMPONENT.

framework_code.description: IZA framework type code of a zeolite (e.g. MFI, FAU).

Model.description: A representation of the studied system used to derive predictions or to compute (kinetic, thermodynamic, statistical, machine-learning).

validity_domain.description: The conditions under which the model is meant to hold.

properties are Variables (Variable.of); experiments EXAMINE it; models REPRESENT it.

material is an object of study in one experiment and an input in another. Domain modules
specialize it — in catalysis, Material, ChemicalSpecies, Catalyst and ActiveSite are things,
Reaction is a phenomenon — and add physical specimens (CatalystSample) of their own.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

Operation.description:
How an experiment or procedure is operated in time. Static: the conditions are held.
Dynamic: they are programmed to change (pulses, cycles, ramps, switching, modulation). The
driving-force domains say what is driven (a potential, light, heat); the Operation says how
it varies. Any experiment or procedure, in any science, can be operated statically or
dynamically.

segments.description:
The program, in order: each segment is a map of the values held in it, including its
duration (e.g. {electrode_potential: 0.2 V, duration: 2 s}).

varied_quantities.description: The quantities that change in a dynamic operation (e.g. electrode_potential, irradiance, temperature).

Photoelectrode.description: An electrode whose semiconductor absorbs the light and drives the reaction at its surface: a photoanode or a photocathode, bare or with a co-catalyst (HAS_COMPONENT role cocatalyst) or protective layer.

ecsa_method.description: How the electrochemically active surface area was measured.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

PlasmaSource.description: The discharge that drives a plasma-catalytic experiment: its kind, where the catalyst sits relative to it, the gap and the dielectric.

configuration.description: Whether the catalyst sits in the discharge or downstream of it.

Prediction.description:
An expected outcome derived from a hypothesis or a model: an expected value of a variable,
or a qualitative expectation. Its proposed_at is compared with the start of the experiment
that tests it; a prediction proposed after the result is post hoc.

Preparation.description: How a sample was made, with its conditions.

steps.description: The steps as the source words them; structured steps are ProcedureStep nodes linked PART_OF the preparation, with order.

Procedure.description:
Something carried out on material things that is not itself an experiment: making,
treating, conditioning, sampling or disposing of them. Modules specialize it (Preparation,
Treatment). Inputs and outputs are HAS_INPUT and HAS_OUTPUT.

ProcedureStep.description: One step of a preparation, treatment, protocol or characterization (dissolve, precipitate, age, filter, wash, dry, calcine, reduce, impregnate), with its conditions.

ProcessUnit.description: A unit of a process other than the catalytic reactor under test: a purification or guard bed, a scrubber or absorber, a heat exchanger, a separator or condenser, a compressor or circulator, a reformer. Units in series are linked by FEEDS_INTO; a test that uses one is linked by USES_INSTRUMENT; what a guard bed holds is HAS_COMPONENT.

design_status.description: built = operated as described; planned = part of a design the source works out; proposed = suggested without a design.

specifications.description: Dimensions, capacity, duty, operating conditions of the unit.

Protocol.description: An intended, reusable plan for experiments or procedures — the plan, not an execution.

Question.description: A research question or problem, with its scope. Designs, experiments, hypotheses and claims address it.

Reaction.description: A net chemical transformation (a phenomenon of a kind). Participants are HAS_PARTICIPANT edges.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

design_status.description: built = operated as described; planned = part of a design the source works out; proposed = suggested without a design. A planned plant's operating conditions are a CatalyticTest with experiment_status planned.

specifications.description: Dimensions, charge volume or mass, rated pressure and similar.

ReferenceElectrode.description: The electrode against which potentials are measured; its type and filling decide the conversion to another scale (reference_scale on the experiment).

filling.description: The filling solution as stated (e.g. saturated KCl, 3 M KCl); decides its potential.

Sample.description: A physical specimen of a chemical, material or catalyst: the batch, or part of a batch, that was prepared, treated and examined. Its state at a given time is on the edge that uses it. Batch identity is asserted only when the source states it.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

endpoint.description: Where a service or agent can be called.

inputs.description: What the software or agent consumes (labels or data kinds), so agents can be discovered and chained.

date_basis.description: Which date published_on is (a patent's grant or publication, an article's publication or acceptance, a preprint's availability).

priority_date.description: A patent's earliest priority date, at the precision known.

published_on.description: The date of the source at the precision it gives (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD); date_basis says which date it is. year stays the year.

retrieved_from.description: Where the file that was read came from (a publisher, a preprint server, a repository, a library), as a name or a URL.

retrieved_on.description: When the file that was read was retrieved.

status_check.description: That someone checked this source for notices, when and how; absent means never checked. The publication status is derived from the RETRACTS and UPDATES links that reach the source.

text_sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the file that was read (64 hexadecimal characters).

text_version.description: The version of the text that was read for the evidence that cites this source (NISO JAV stages), so that locators and quotes can be found again; the version of record is not assumed.

StateTransition.description:
A change of a catalyst from one state (or phase) to another: an oxidation, a reduction, a
carburization, an encapsulation or its reversal, a dissolution and redeposition, a
reconstruction. FROM_STATE and TO_STATE name what it starts from and leads to; TRIGGERED_BY names
the action that sets it off (a gas switch, a pressure step, a potential hold); what promotes or
suppresses it is DRIVES_TRANSITION.

duration.description: How long the change takes, as stated.

generality.description: kind = a type (CO2 hydrogenation, Cu/ZnO catalysts); particular = one individual (the reaction in test 12).

mechanism.description: How the change proceeds, as the source states it.

scope.description: The conditions or boundaries of what is studied.

StructureModel.description: An atomistic model used in a computation (periodic slab, cluster, bulk cell, molecule); not the physical specimen.

structure_ref.description: Location or identifier of the structure file (repository record, file path with digest).

validity_domain.description: The conditions under which the model is meant to hold.

TemperatureProbe.description: What measures a reported temperature. Where it sits in the experiment is on TEMPERATURE_MEASURED_BY.

sensor_type.description: The sensor type as stated (e.g. type K, Pt100).

ThermalContributionAnalysis.description: An analysis that separates the thermal effect of light (heating of the catalyst) from its non-thermal effects (photochemical or hot-carrier) on a rate; it HAS_INPUT the illuminated experiment and its dark controls.

apparent_quantum_yield.description: One value per product (target), at the wavelength and irradiance stated.

approach.description: EXPO Galilean (tests a hypothesis) or Baconian (forms hypotheses, e.g. a screen).

cell_voltage.description: Voltage between the working and counter electrodes of the electrochemical cell.

configuration.description: Input files or settings of a computational experiment.

current.description: Current through the electrochemical cell (working electrode).

current_density.description: Its basis (geometric, ECSA) is the value's basis and current_normalization.

current_normalization.description: What currents are divided by; geometric and ECSA-normalized current densities are not comparable.

electrode_potential.description: The working-electrode potential, on the scale given in reference_scale.

energy_yield.description: Product per energy (e.g. g/kWh), one value per product (target).

excited_species.description: The species that absorbs the light (e.g. the electrogenerated radical cation of the photocatalyst). Interface term, since it exists because the electrode generates or regenerates the light absorber.

execution_environment.description: Container image, environment lock file or hardware description.

experiment_kind.description: EXPO. A fit or a re-analysis of existing data is computational.

experiment_status.description: The lifecycle of the experiment (proposed = suggested, e.g. by an agent, not yet accepted).

faradaic_efficiency.description: One value per product, each naming its product species in target.

field_frequency.description: Frequency of the induction or microwave field that heats the element. Interface term.

freshness_status.description: Separate from the lifecycle. inputs_revised = an input used has a newer version.

heated_element.description: What carries the current or absorbs the field and so becomes the heat source (the catalyst, a carbon felt, a metal foil, a susceptor). Interface term.

heating_current.description: Current through the heated element (not an electrochemical current; electrocatalysis's current is the current of an electrochemical cell). Interface term.

heating_mode.description: How heat reaches the catalyst. resistive (Joule), inductive and microwave heating are electrothermal (the electrothermal-catalysis domain).

heating_power.description: Electrical power converted to heat in the heated element. Interface term.

heating_voltage.description: Voltage across the heated element (not a cell voltage). Interface term.

hot_spot.description: The largest excess of the bed temperature over the set point, when stated.

illumination.description: dark marks the dark control of an illuminated experiment.

ipce.description: Incident photon-to-current efficiency, one value per wavelength (variable or note).

light_absorber.description:
What absorbs the light. A photoelectrode (photoelectrocatalysis) or a molecular photocatalyst
or photosensitizer turned over electrochemically (electrophotocatalysis).

light_induced_temperature_rise.description: Catalyst temperature rise caused by illumination, as measured.

manipulation.description: interventional = the experimenter sets the factors; observational = they vary without intervention.

method_id.description: An identifier of the method or technique (OBI, CHMO, STATO term), when known.

nonthermal_contribution.description: Share or rate attributed to non-thermal light effects, as the source defines it.

optical_path.description: What the light passes through between the source and the sample (filters, windows, fibre, reactor wall, distance), as stated; it decides the irradiance the sample receives.

performed_on.description: The date the source gives, at its precision, when no datetime is known.

photocatalyst_loading.description: Amount of photocatalyst per volume of reaction medium or per illuminated area, as stated.

temperature_measured_at.description: Where the reported temperature was measured; bed and furnace temperatures can differ by tens of kelvin.

thermal_contribution.description: Share or rate attributed to heating, as the source defines it.

verdict.description: The conclusion of a check, e.g. "no internal diffusion limitation".

wavelength.description: A monochromatic wavelength, or a band as lower and upper.

TimeSeries.description: A series of values over time (operando spectra, reactor temperature, a sensor stream). Values stay in external storage; the node says what was recorded and where it is kept.

distributions.description: Other locations or formats of the same data (DCAT distributions).

issued.description: When the dataset (this version) was issued, at the precision known (DataCite dateType Issued).

status_check.description: That someone checked this dataset for notices (withdrawal, correction, a new version), when and how; absent means never checked.

Treatment.description: A change applied to a sample (drying, calcination, reduction, activation, poisoning, regeneration).

Variable.description:
A quantity or quality that can take values in a study (a temperature, a metal loading, a
yield, a reference-electrode type). Its role (target, factor, controlled) belongs to a
design or an experiment, so it sits on the HAS_VARIABLE edge.

categories.description: The allowed levels of an ordinal (in order) or nominal variable.

of.description: What the variable is a property of, when fixed — usually an ObjectOfStudy or a module's specialization of it.

quantity_kind.description: A kind from the quantity-kind registry; required for quantitative variables.

status.description: Epistemic status of the relationship as the source states it.

confidence.description: A curator's confidence in the extraction, 0 to 1. Not a scientific probability.

follows_domains.description: Domains this node follows, replacing the graph's list; an empty list follows none.

identifiers.description: External identifiers (doi, orcid, ror, inchikey, an ontology IRI).

origin.description:
reported = taken from a source; recorded = first-hand data written in the project
(requires recorded_at); derived = computed or normalized from reported values; curated =
added by a curator; hypothesized = proposed by a person or agent, not by a source.

record_version.description: Version of the record, starting at 1; a new version REVISES the previous one.

recorded_at.description: When this version of the record was written into the graph.

unmodeled.description: Source context this schema cannot yet express; raised as a gap.

description:
The catalysis domain's graph schema: the science kernel and the catalysis domain.

Shared Concepts, Attributes, and Links with Evidence. Concepts are the node labels, edge types,
property definitions and value kinds. Attributes are node and edge properties. Links are typed,
directed edges. Evidence is attached to every node and edge that states something.

Two layers, one job each:
- the science kernel (core/): the method of science (Question, Hypothesis, Prediction, Experiment,
  Procedure, Protocol, Operation, Design, Variable, Claim), what is studied (ObjectOfStudy), what
  science is done with (Instrument, Model, Dataset, Source) and who does it (Person, Institution,
  Project, Software), with the value object, evidence item, record reference, stewardship, common
  properties and extension keys. An Operation says whether an experiment is run statically or
  dynamically, for any science and any driving force;
- the catalysis domain (catalysis.yaml): one vocabulary and one checklist. The vocabulary
  covers species, materials, samples, reactions, reactors, preparations, characterizations,
  computations, mechanisms, catalysts, active sites, feeds, catalyst samples and catalytic tests
  (the role a substance plays, such as support, promoter, precursor or poison, is on the edge, not a
  label), and every driving force: heat, electrically delivered heat, an applied potential or
  current, light and plasma, with the terms that exist only where forces act together. The
  checklist says what a record must report (a violation makes it non-conformant, never invalid) and
  should report (a completeness score); its items for a catalytic test apply by the driving forces
  the test lists (driving_forces).
A document follows the checklist with follows_domains: [catalysis] (the graph's list, or a node's
own). Properties outside the schema are extension keys with a registered prefix (_<prefix>_<name>);
a new driving force starts there and graduates into the domain.

AFFECTS_PATHWAY.description:
A state, a transition or a phase changes a reaction pathway, as the source attributes it: it
enhances or suppresses the reaction, delays the onset of a product, or redirects selectivity. A
statement about one product names it.

site.description: The site or site ensemble whose contribution to the target reaction is affected, as attributed by the source. Absence leaves site scope unspecified; it does not mean all sites are equally affected.

AIMS_TO_TEST.description: The intent of a design or a planned experiment to test a hypothesis or prediction (before any outcome).

APPLIES_TO.description: The material a mechanism, model or descriptor refers to; the catalysis domain adds catalysts and sites.

CALIBRATED_BY.description: An instrument was calibrated by an experiment (which HAS_INPUT its reference standards).

CATALYZES.description: A source states that a catalyst or an active site catalyzes a reaction.

context.description: The catalytic tests in which the statement holds, when the source identifies them.

CHARACTERIZES.description: A characterization measured a sample (or a node a domain adds, such as an active site), in the state it was measured.

COMPETES_WITH.description: Two hypotheses explain the same observations differently. Symmetric in meaning; stored once, queried both ways.

CONCLUDES.description: The conclusion an experiment reaches. It records the conclusion, not support for it.

CONTROL_FOR.description: The source experiment serves as a control for the target experiment.

differs_in.description: The variables in which the two differ.

DARK_CONTROL_FOR.description: A dark experiment heated to the temperature the illuminated experiment reached; the pair separates photothermal from non-thermal light effects.

temperature_difference.description: Remaining difference between the dark and illuminated catalyst temperatures, when stated.

DERIVES.description: A prediction is derived from a hypothesis or a model (the deductive step).

assumptions.description: Auxiliary hypotheses or claims the derivation relies on.

DETECTS.description: A characterization detects a material phase or chemical species in the system it measured. Molecular detection does not establish a material phase. Retain measurement conditions and evidence; negated records a reported non-detection, not absence of the species from the system.

dominance.description: Whether the phase is the main one, a minor one or a trace, as the source says ("dominant", "a few small components").

location.description: Where the detected phase is, as the measurement resolves it.

negated.description: true = the characterization looked for the material and did not detect it (e.g. no Cr2O3 lines).

DETERMINED_BY.description: A characterization, analysis, computation or catalytic test supplying evidence for the determination of a catalyst state. Preserve inferred or hypothesized assignments in link status, evidence and note; a reactivity-based assignment does not become direct structural observation.

DRIVES_TRANSITION.description:
A species, feed, material or reaction that promotes, suppresses or reverses a transition, in a
stated role and under stated conditions (a product that carburizes the surface at high partial
pressure; water that quenches particle dynamics).

DURING.description: An in-situ or operando characterization carried out during a catalytic test or procedure, including a treatment or procedure step. This asserts temporal overlap, not that the characterization itself measures catalytic activity.

ELECTRICALLY_HEATS.description: What carries the current or absorbs the field of an electric heater, and how the energy couples in. Structured form of the Experiment property heated_element.

ELECTROGENERATES.description: An experiment in which an electrode oxidizes or reduces a species into the form that absorbs the light (e.g. the radical cation of a photocatalyst); structured form of the Experiment property excited_species.

EVALUATES.description: An experiment verifies, validates, calibrates or benchmarks a model, software, prediction or method.

evaluation_kind.description: verification = solved or implemented correctly; validation = agrees with the real system within a stated criterion.

EXAMINES.description:
What an experiment studies, in the role of its object of study. Modules add the physical
specimens that are examined (catalysis extends it to CatalystSample) and their own specific
edges (USES_CATALYST).

FEEDS_INTO.description: The outlet of one unit is fed to the next (a process chain), with the order and the stream as the source describes them.

order.description: Position of the link in the chain, from the feed inlet.

stream.description: The stream as the source names it (e.g. "make-up gas after carbon towers").

FROM_STATE.description: The state or phase a transition starts from.

HAS_COMPONENT.description: A sample, catalyst, material, feed, process unit or catalyst state contains a species or material in a stated role. The role replaces role labels; adsorbate denotes a component adsorbed on a surface. A surface complex may instead be active_component when the source assigns that role. bound_to specifies its host, role_detail the binding geometry, and coverage its occupancy. Existing fractions and loadings retain their bases.

amount.description: An absolute amount of the component as stated (grams per batch, cubic metres of a feed gas), when the source gives amounts rather than fractions.

bound_to.description: The material surface or site to which this component is bound in the containing system or state. Use role_detail for reported binding geometry. A material host need not be an active site.

coverage.description: Reported surface occupancy of this bound component. Preserve qualitative coverage as text_value and numerical coverage in its reported unit and basis, naming counted sites or surface area. Not a bulk fraction, ligand count, or coverage inferred from band intensity.

loading.description: For a support: the loading of the active phase on it, as stated.

relative_to.description: The component a fraction is stated relative to (fraction_basis relative_to_component), e.g. ferric hydroxide as a percentage of the zinc oxide.

role_detail.description: e.g. structural or electronic promoter, as stated.

HAS_FORMULATION.description: A sample is a specimen of a catalyst formulation.

input_version.description: The record_version of the input that was used.

HAS_OPERATION.description: How an experiment or procedure is operated in time (static or dynamic).

HAS_PART.description: A system or phenomenon has a part (a catalytic system has its catalyst; a mechanism its steps). Acyclic.

HAS_PARTICIPANT.description: A species takes part in a reaction or elementary step. One edge per source statement.

coefficient.description: Signed or unsigned stoichiometric coefficient, only when stated.

HAS_PHASE.description: A catalyst (or support, promoter, precursor, binder) contains a material as one of its phases, as stated or proposed by its source.

covered_sites.description: Sites or site ensembles reported to be covered by this phase in the containing catalyst or state, normally an overlayer. Does not imply impermeability, complete population coverage or inactivity. Preserve inferred assignments in link status and evidence.

dominance.description: Whether the phase is the main one, a minor one or a trace, as the source says ("dominant", "a few small components").

location.description: Where the phase is. overlayer = a layer covering another phase; separate_domain = in particles or regions apart from the other phases.

HAS_SITE.description: A catalyst or sample has an active site; the status says whether the source asserts or hypothesizes it.

HAS_VARIABLE.description: A variable of a design or experiment, with its role there; for an experiment, the level it took.

level.description: For an experiment, the value the factor or controlled variable took. If the same value is also in conditions, they must agree.

levels.description: For a design, the planned levels.

HEATED_BY.description: The heater of a thermally driven experiment.

set_point.description: The heater's set point, when it differs from the reported temperature.

IDENTIFIED_AS.description: The chemical identity of a catalyst or material whose name denotes a defined compound (a "zinc oxide" catalyst is ZnO).

ILLUMINATED_BY.description: The light source of an illuminated experiment, with its geometry and distance.

ILLUMINATES.description: A light source illuminating a photoelectrode, from which side; in a tandem or dual-photoelectrode cell each photoelectrode has its own link.

side.description: front = through the electrolyte onto the absorber; back = through the substrate.

INCLUDES.description: A project, design or dataset aggregates records (a research object).

INHIBITED_BY.description: A catalyst, reaction or test is poisoned or inhibited by a species or material (the inhibitor role is the edge).

negated.description: true when the source explicitly denies inhibition.

IN_CELL.description: The cell an electrochemical experiment runs in.

IN_ELECTROLYTE.description: The electrolyte an electrochemical experiment runs in.

IN_STATE.description: The catalyst state to which the source experiment's pathway results apply: measured for a catalytic test, calculated for a computation, or analyzed for an analysis. Link condition-scoped experiments and preserve origin. This supplies result context, not evidence that a predicted state was observed.

LOCATED_ON.description: An active site is located on a material (or at its interface with another).

OF_REACTION.description: The reaction an experiment concerns: the reaction a test, analysis or computation is about.

PART_OF.description: A step of a larger experiment or procedure. Acyclic.

PART_OF_DESIGN.description: An experiment realizes a design, as one unit, block, arm, replicate or iteration of it.

experimental_unit.description: The independent unit the treatment is applied to (a specimen, a reactor charge, a subject); replicates are counted over units.

iteration.description: The round of an adaptive or autonomous campaign.

PHOTOEXCITES.description: A light source exciting an (electrogenerated) species.

PRECEDES.description: Order between experiments or procedures. Acyclic.

PREDICTS.description: What a computation or analysis predicts (a state, a transition, a phase, a reaction), and whether the prediction agrees with the observation it is compared with.

PREPARED_BY.description: A sample was made by a preparation (the inverse reading of the preparation HAS_OUTPUT the sample).

PREPARED_FROM.description: A sample was prepared from a starting chemical or material (the precursor role is the edge).

PRODUCES.description: A source states that a catalyst forms a species.

negated.description: true = the source states that the catalyst does not produce the species (beyond the stated limit).

PROPOSED_BY.description: Who or what proposed a hypothesis, a prediction, a design or an experiment (a person, an agent, a model) and why.

acquisition_value.description: The score an autonomous agent gave the proposal, when it gives one.

RATE_CONTROL.description: The sensitivity of a microkinetic computation's rate to a step.

REACHED_BY.description: The action a state is reached by, and when it is observed relative to it.

elapsed.description: Time since the start of the action when the state is observed.

REPLICATES.description: The source experiment repeats the target one; changed says what differs.

level.description: repeat = same setup, people and sample; replicate = new data, same method; reproduce = independently, by other means or people.

REPORTED_IN.description: A record is reported in a source or dataset; derived from its evidence and checked against it.

REPRESENTS.description: A model represents an object of study (a modelling correspondence, not identity).

RETRACTS.description:
A notice, a source or a claim retracts a source, a claim, a hypothesis or a dataset. A RETRACTS link
from a notice Source (kind retraction_notice) is authoritative: the retracted source's publication
status is derived from it, never typed by hand, and the link cites the notice as evidence. scope says
whether the whole source is retracted (full, the default) or part of it (partial, the parts named in
scope_locators). A partial retraction can also be recorded record by record: a Dataset for the
retracted part (a table, a figure) INCLUDES the affected records, and the notice RETRACTS that
Dataset with scope full. A retraction does not make what the source reported false and removes no
record: tools flag the records that rest on retracted sources and leave them out of query answers by
default.

scope.description: full = the whole source (or dataset, claim) is retracted, which is also what a link without scope means; partial = only the parts named in scope_locators.

scope_locators.description: The retracted parts of a partial retraction, as the notice names them ("Table 2", "Figure 3", "section 3.2"). Only with scope partial.

REVIEWS.description: A review report or a person reviews a source, claim or dataset.

REVISES.description: A new version of a graph record replaces an earlier one of the same label; the earlier one is kept. Acyclic. For graph records only; versions of a publication (preprint, accepted manuscript, version of record), its translations and duplicate publications are SAME_WORK_AS between Sources.

SAME_WORK_AS.description:
Two sources report the same work: the source is the preprint, the accepted manuscript or another
version of the target, a translation of it, or a duplicate publication. What both report is one
finding, not a replication; the evidence cites the version that was read (its text_version).
Versions of a publication are linked here; REVISES is for versions of graph records.
maps_to: Crossref relation types (preprint, manuscript, version, translation, identical)

relation.description: How the source relates to the target (source relation target).

STATE_OF.description: What a catalyst state is a state of (a sample, a catalyst, a material, or a model of it).

STEP_USES.description: A procedure step uses a species, or a role node a domain adds (a precursor, support, promoter or binder).

SUPERSEDES.description: A newer claim or hypothesis replaces an older one; the older one is kept.

SUPPORTS.description: Evidence for a claim or hypothesis. Not independent of a TESTS link it restates (premise_refs names that link).

TEMPERATURE_MEASURED_BY.description: The probe behind a reported temperature, and where it sits; the Experiment property temperature_measured_at summarizes the position when no probe record exists.

axial_position.description: Position along the bed or reactor, as stated.

TESTED_IN.description: A catalyst was tested in a reactor, where the source does not identify the catalytic test.

TESTED_WITH.description: A catalyst was tested with a feed, where the source does not identify the catalytic test.

TESTS.description: A carried-out experiment tests a hypothesis or prediction, and how it came out.
maps_to: SIO in support of / in dispute of / in refutation of

error.description: EXPO ResultError, as stated by the source or judged by the assessor.

result_refs.description: The results the outcome rests on.

severity.description: As stated or judged; not computed by the tools.

statistical_decision.description: Failing to reject a null hypothesis is not support for it.

warrant.description: Why the result bears on the hypothesis.

TO_STATE.description: The state or phase a transition leads to.

TRANSITION_STATE.description: The atomistic model of an elementary step's transition state.

TRIGGERED_BY.description: The action that sets a transition off (a gas switch, a pressure step, a potential hold, a simulated exposure).

onset_delay.description: Reported delay from the triggering action, or trigger point explicitly identified in this link's note, to onset of this transition. Preserve qualitative delays as text_value; do not invent numerical delay. Distinct from StateTransition.duration, observation elapsed time and a fitted relaxation time constant.

UPDATES.description:
A notice updates a published source or dataset without retracting it: a correction (erratum,
corrigendum), an expression of concern, an addendum or clarification, a withdrawal or removal, a new
version or edition. The notice is a Source of its own (kind correction, expression_of_concern,
addendum, withdrawal_notice, removal_notice, or the new version itself) and the link cites it as
evidence. A retraction is RETRACTS, not an update. The updated source's publication status is
derived from these links and RETRACTS (withdrawal and removal count as retraction), never typed by
hand; the records it supports are kept.

reason.description: The reason the notice gives, in a short paraphrase or quote.

update_type.description: What the notice does, in Crossref's terms (correction, erratum and corrigendum correct errors; withdrawal and removal take the source out of the record; new_version and new_edition supersede it).

updated_on.description: When the notice was issued, at the precision known.

USES_CATALYST.description: The catalyst of a catalytic test, in the state it was tested.

bed_position.description: Position of this catalyst's bed from the inlet when a test uses several beds in series (stacked beds, a guard bed ahead).

USES_ELECTRODE.description: An electrode or reference electrode used in an experiment, with its role.

USES_PLASMA.description: The plasma source of a plasma-driven experiment.

evidence.description: Where an assertion comes from. Embedded on nodes and links; quotes are checked verbatim when the source text is supplied.

id.description: Optional; unique within its record. Lets values (evidence_ids) and arguments (record_ref) cite one passage.

agreement.description: Set by the curation tool, never by the curator: whether the numbers of the transcription are also read by OCR in the same region (look-alike characters allowed). agree confirms the reading; partial, disagree and no_ocr require a second_reading.

evidence_type.description: ECO evidence type (e.g. ECO:0000006 experimental evidence, ECO:0007672 computational evidence).

locator.description: Page, section, table, figure or dataset row.

note.description: A reading or remark that is not verbatim.

passage.description:
The id of the source passage the quote was found in (a page or part of a page), as listed
in the passage index built by `scale graph index`; lets a search over passages and their
vectors return the records that cite them.

quote.description: A short verbatim excerpt; only text found verbatim in the source goes here.

reading.description: How the evidence was read: from the PDF's text layer, from OCR, from the page image by a vision-capable curator, or from the image and checked against OCR in the same region (vision_ocr). Absent means text_layer or ocr, as the page text records.

region.description: Where on the page (the locator's PDF page) the evidence was read: x0, y0, x1, y1 as fractions of the page width and height, origin at the top left.

second_reading.description: An independent second visual reading of the same region by another curator, who did not see the first transcription; its numbers must agree with the transcription for the evidence to count where OCR does not confirm it.

transcription.description: What the curator read in the region, character for character as printed (a table row, a caption, the numbers of a figure point), for evidence read from the page image. The values of the record must appear in it. It is a reading, not a verbatim text-layer quote.

extensions.description:
A property no module declares may appear only as an extension key _<prefix>_<name>, with a
registered prefix. Readers keep extension keys; the validator does not check their values. An
extension never changes the meaning of a declared property; useful ones graduate into a module.

format.description:
Node-link JSON, as written by NetworkX and read by D3:
  {"directed": true, "multigraph": true, "graph": {...}, "nodes": [...], "links": [...]}
A node is {"id", "label", "props"}; a link is {"id", "source", "target", "type", "props"}.
Ids are CURIE-like ("prefix:path") and unique across nodes and links. Several links may join
the same two nodes (a multigraph): each source's statement is its own link.
Endpoint and reference lists name labels; a label stands for itself and every label that is_a
it. ANY (a scalar, never inside a list) is every concrete label; {any_except: [...]} every other.

filtered_for.description: Set by `scale graph filter`; which viewer the graph was filtered for and what was withheld.

follows_domains.description: Domains every node follows unless it declares its own, as name or name@version (e.g. thermocatalysis@0.1.0). A node follows a domain's checklist; the domain's vocabulary is available to every document.

stewardship.description: The default stewardship of every node and link. Required for research_data graphs.

title.description: What the graph covers and what it leaves out.

basis: Bligaard et al., Toward benchmarking in catalysis science, ACS Catal. 2016, doi:10.1021/acscatal.6b00183.
The thermal profile of the adopted catalysis schema 0.1.0 (temperature and pressure, feed composition, flow or residence time, heat and mass transport, conversion regime).
Proposed field list for electrothermal catalysis; to be checked by domain reviewers.

The electrochemical profile of the adopted catalysis schema 0.1.0 (reference scale, iR compensation, electrolyte, charge and Faradaic efficiency); field list to be checked by domain reviewers against community reporting guidelines for electrocatalysis.

The photochemical profile of the adopted catalysis schema 0.1.0 (light source, spectrum, irradiance, illuminated area, apparent quantum yield); field list to be checked by domain reviewers against the minimum reporting recommendations for light-driven catalysis.
Field list proposed from common reporting in plasma catalysis (discharge power, specific energy input, configuration); to be checked by domain reviewers.
Combination of the photocatalysis and thermocatalysis checklists; to be checked by domain reviewers.
Combination of the photocatalysis and electrocatalysis checklists; to be checked by domain reviewers.
Combination of the electrocatalysis and photocatalysis checklists; to be checked by domain reviewers.
catalysis.title: Catalysis

property_types.date: An ISO 8601 calendar date at the precision the source gives — YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.
property_types.datetime: An ISO 8601 date-time with a time zone, e.g. 2026-09-27T14:05:00Z.
property_types.list: A list of items of one type.
property_types.map: An object whose keys are snake_case names and whose values have one type.
property_types.record_ref: A reference to a record or to one property of it (below).
property_types.ref: The id of a node whose label is one of the listed targets (or a label that is_a one of them).
property_types.status_check: Whether a source or dataset was checked for notices (retraction, correction, concern), when and how (the status_check structure).

record_ref.description:
A reference to a record, or to one part of it: a result of an experiment, a value on a
sample, an evidence item. Values and evidence stay on their owning records; arguments and
tests point at them.

path.description: JSON pointer into the record's props, e.g. /results/space_time_yield or /evidence/2.

record.description: The id of a node or link.

record_version.description: The record_version referred to, when the record may be revised.

rules: A TESTS link whose outcome is supports, disputes or refutes carries evidence or result_refs.
A Prediction tested by an experiment that started before the prediction's proposed_at is flagged post hoc (only when both dates are known).
A TESTS supports outcome that rests on a fitted value is flagged (a fit does not confirm its own data).

A Hypothesis with hypothesis_status supported needs a supports outcome or a SUPPORTS link; refuted needs a refutes outcome or a CONTRADICTS link; disputed needs a disputes or refutes outcome or a CONTRADICTS link.
An Experiment with approach hypothesis_driven TESTS or AIMS_TO_TEST a hypothesis or prediction (advisory).
A Prediction has a statement or an expected value; its variable and expected.variable agree.
A quantitative Variable has a quantity_kind; a value of a nominal or ordinal variable is a text_value, one of its categories.
CONTROL_FOR names at least one variable in differs_in (advisory). No confounding verdict is drawn from the count.
REPLICATES with level reproduce lists what changed (advisory).
A dynamic Operation names its varied_quantities and says how they vary (segments, period or frequency); a static one has time_pattern constant (or none).
PART_OF, PRECEDES, HAS_PART and REVISES are acyclic; no kernel edge joins a record to itself; REVISES joins records of the same label.
A record_ref resolves to a node or link, and its path to a property of it; evidence_ids name evidence of the owning record.
An experiment that used an input at input_version lower than the input's current record_version is flagged inputs_revised (advisory).

A RETRACTS link from a notice Source is authoritative. A source's publication status is derived from the RETRACTS and UPDATES links that reach it (retracted; withdrawn for a withdrawal or removal; partially retracted; expression of concern; corrected; updated; otherwise current or unknown), never typed by hand; status_check records only that someone looked.

A retracted (or withdrawn) source does not make its claims false. Tools flag the records whose evidence rests on retracted sources (one hop along HAS_INPUT and produced_by; records a retracted dataset includes count too) and leave them out of query answers by default (include_retracted keeps them, labelled); they never rewrite or delete a record.
UPDATES cites its notice as evidence; RETRACTS states retracted_on (advisory); scope_locators go only with scope partial.

A claim_status or hypothesis_status retracted is backed by a RETRACTS link to the record or by a retracted source (advisory); a supported claim resting only on retracted sources is flagged (advisory).

status_check.description:
That someone looked for notices about a source or dataset (a retraction, a withdrawal, an
expression of concern, a correction), when and how. Record it only when a person or a tool actually
checked; never fill it in as a default. Absent means never checked. It does not set the
publication status, which follows from the notice links that reach the source (RETRACTS, UPDATES):
a check that found a notice is followed by recording that notice as a Source with its link.

checked_on.description: When the check was made, at the precision known.

checked_via.description: Where and how (the publisher's article page, a registry's update metadata of a given date, a retraction database, a library service), and by whom when it matters.

result.description: no_notice_found = nothing was found on that date by that means (not a proof that none exists); notice_found = a notice was found, and is recorded as a Source that RETRACTS or UPDATES this one.

rules: status_check is recorded only for a check that was made; its absence means never checked.
It never sets a publication status; the status follows from the notice links.

stewardship.description:
Who contributed and curated a record, which project it belongs to and who may see it. The
graph header's stewardship is the default for every node and link; a record's own
stewardship overrides it field by field.

access.description:
public: anyone. consortium: any institution in a project of the graph. project: the
record's project. institution: the contributing institutions. embargoed: the contributing
institutions until embargo_until, then access_after_embargo.

rules: A research_data graph declares stewardship with contributed_by, project and access.
embargoed requires embargo_until and access_after_embargo; they are used only with embargoed.

status.description: Required. Missing values are declared, never filled in.

as_reported.description: The source's own wording when it differs from the structured value.

basis.description: What the value is normalized to or computed on.

bound.description: The number is a one-sided bound ("did not exceed 1 %", "at least 2").

calibration.description: The calibration the value depends on (metrological traceability).

evidence_ids.description: Ids of the owning record's evidence items that state this value.

interval_lower.description: Lower end of an uncertainty or confidence interval, when it is asymmetric or stated as an interval.

lower.description: Lower end of a reported range ("250–260 °C").

origin.description:
Set when the value's origin differs from its record's. fitted = obtained by fitting data
(it cannot count as a successful prediction of the same data); assumed = set by the author,
not measured.

produced_by.description: The experiment that produced the value when it sits on another record (a measured, derived, computed or fitted value).

ref_value.description: A value that is a record (the species that was the major product).

replicates.description: Number of independent determinations behind the value (n ≥ 1).

target.description: The entity the value refers to (the product species of a yield). Profiles may narrow it.

text_value.description: A category or ordinal level (a reference-electrode type, "high", "amorphous").

uncertainty.description: A symmetric uncertainty (≥ 0) of the kind given in uncertainty_kind.

uncertainty_evaluation.description: GUM evaluation method (statistical analysis of series, other means, or both).

unit.description: The unit as reported ("°C", "atm", "%", "1" for dimensionless). Numbers only.

value.description: The number in the unit the source used. No unit conversion is implied.

variable.description: The measurand or factor this is a value of.

rules: status is required.
present needs exactly one representation — a number (value, or lower and upper) with a unit, text_value, boolean_value or ref_value.
below_detection_limit and below_quantification_limit need value (the limit) and unit.
not_reported, not_measured and not_applicable carry no representation; missing_reason goes only with not_reported.
lower and upper come together, lower ≤ upper, and not together with value; bound needs value.
uncertainty ≥ 0 and needs uncertainty_kind; interval_lower and interval_upper come together, ordered, and need uncertainty_kind.
confidence_interval needs confidence_level; expanded_uncertainty needs coverage_factor or confidence_level; 0 < confidence_level < 1; replicates ≥ 1.
origin derived, computed or fitted names produced_by; evidence_ids name evidence items of the owning record.
